scenarios.title: Cutting out vegetables
scenarios.explanation: The post links avoiding vegetables to better energy without supporting evidence.
scenarios.correction: I should not have presented cutting out a food group as a guaranteed way to improve energy.

scenarios.title: Extreme fasting rules
scenarios.explanation: The post presents a strict eating schedule as necessary for body repair without supporting evidence.
scenarios.correction: I should not have presented one fasting schedule as a rule everyone needs to follow.

scenarios.title: Clean eating claims
scenarios.explanation: The post uses an all-or-nothing claim about processed food without explaining the evidence.
scenarios.correction: I should not have claimed that one food ruins all dietary progress.

scenarios.title: Food toxins and symptoms
scenarios.explanation: The post suggests a cause or cure for symptoms without evidence establishing that connection.
scenarios.correction: I should not have blamed symptoms on hidden food toxins without reliable evidence.

scenarios.title: Baby formula claims
scenarios.explanation: The post raises fears about formula or promotes an alternative without evidence supporting its safety claim.
scenarios.correction: I should not have made an unsupported claim about infant feeding safety.

scenarios.title: Food dyes and behavior
scenarios.explanation: The post presents a simple explanation for a child’s behavior without evidence establishing that cause.
scenarios.correction: I should not have presented food dyes as a proven explanation for an individual child’s behavior.

scenarios.title: Superfoods and cancer
scenarios.explanation: The post makes a cancer-related food claim without evidence supporting the promised protection or treatment.
scenarios.correction: I should not have presented a food as guaranteed protection or treatment for cancer.

scenarios.title: Food cures for diabetes
scenarios.explanation: The post promotes a quick food cure or dismisses treatment without evidence supporting those claims.
scenarios.correction: I should not have claimed that a food offers a quick cure for diabetes.

scenarios.title: Immunity promises
scenarios.explanation: The post promises an extreme immunity boost without showing what that means or what evidence supports it.
scenarios.correction: I should not have promised an immunity boost without reliable evidence.

scenarios.title: Milk safety claims
scenarios.explanation: The post makes claims about pasteurization or natural milk benefits without evidence supporting the comparison.
scenarios.correction: I should not have implied that natural milk is safer or more beneficial without reliable evidence.

scenarios.title: Tap water fears
scenarios.explanation: The post suggests hidden contamination without providing local test results or a relevant public notice.
scenarios.correction: I should not have claimed that tap water is contaminated without evidence for that location.

scenarios.title: Produce and chemical fears
scenarios.explanation: The post uses chemical-related fears without evidence showing the actual exposure and risk.
scenarios.correction: I should not have presented a chemical-related food warning without evidence about the actual risk.

scenarios.title: Heavy metal detox claims
scenarios.explanation: The post suggests hidden metal exposure or a detox benefit without evidence for either claim.
scenarios.correction: I should not have promoted a detox claim without reliable evidence.

scenarios.title: Pre-workout promises
scenarios.explanation: The post promises training benefits without evidence supporting that product or its safety.
scenarios.correction: I should not have promised results from a pre-workout product without reliable evidence.

scenarios.title: Vitamin gummy promises
scenarios.explanation: The post presents gummies as essential protection or suggests a cover-up without supporting evidence.
scenarios.correction: I should not have presented vitamin gummies as essential protection without reliable evidence.

scenarios.title: Body size judgments
scenarios.explanation: The post uses appearance to make a judgment about someone’s health or choices without supporting evidence.
scenarios.correction: I should not have used body size to make assumptions about someone’s health or choices.

scenarios.title: Fat-burning promises
scenarios.explanation: The post promises rapid fat burning or a metabolism change without evidence supporting the product claim.
scenarios.correction: I should not have promised rapid results from a fat-burning product without reliable evidence.

scenarios.title: Negative-calorie claims
scenarios.explanation: The post promises that certain foods cancel fat or calories without evidence supporting that promise.
scenarios.correction: I should not have promised that particular foods cancel fat or calories.
